method: Shokri et al. S&P'17 shadow-model MIA
limitations: MIA target is a LoRA-style linear probe over frozen private-base features (standard lightweight MIA target); it models the output-confidence channel the mask affects, not a full attention/MLP LoRA.
Black-box outputs-only attacker; a white-box or per-example-gradient attacker is out of this channel.
Absolute AUC is modest because the fine-tune is light and SST-2 generalizes well (small member gap); we report the RELATIVE channel comparison, which is the design-relevant quantity.
Protected channels are modeled at the 2-class verbalizer boundary via the S3 monomial mask; a full vocab-logit MIA would see the same set-symmetric preservation (perm-only) shown in S3.

interpretation.membership_signal_source: the fine-tuned head's over-confidence on members (generalization gap); a property of training, NOT of the mask.
interpretation.masking_effect: the mask only changes READABILITY of the output confidence. perm-only preserves the set-symmetric confidence (maxprob/entropy) so most of the black-box signal remains; monomial distorts it, reducing readable signal; neither removes membership leakage at its source (the trained weights).
